subject: Next steps: SDK quickstart, tool-calling & embeddings test harness
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightpath.ai>, Devon Lee <devon@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: SDK quickstart, tool-calling & embeddings test harness

Thanks for the demo earlier — really helpful context. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary use case: structured triage assistant inside Acme's clinician portal (short prompts + tool calling to fetch patient context).
- Constraints: PII must stay in their VPC for retrieval layer; service latency target 200–300ms p95 for interactive flows.
- Priority features: SDK-based local testing kit, authenticated routing to private deployment, embeddings for semantic search + a light reranker.

Proposed immediate actions (this week)
1) SDK quickstart bundle: I attached a one-page quickstart (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md) that walks through Python + TS installs, auth with API key vs. short-lived signed tokens, and a local sample that calls a fake patient-db. Please try the Python example in the repo.
2) Tool-calling spec: see sample-toolcall-spec.json attachment — suggests a minimal /tool/resolve patient API stub you can run locally. This will let the front-end prototype exercise structured outputs.
3) Embeddings pilot: small test harness (100–200 records) to validate vectorization and reranker behavior. We can run this in your sandbox or via a dedicated private pod.
4) Network checklist: Devon, your network diagram (thanks) flagged two firewall rules needed for the private agent to reach our control plane. Please confirm we can open outbound to *.redwood.ai:443 from the pilot subnet.

Scheduling
- Can we meet Thursday 10am PT for a 30-minute tech workshop to walk through the quickstart and run the first local demo together?

Deliverables we will send after this note
- A minimal sample app repo (Python + TS sample) with auth stubs and the tool-call example.
- A prefilled mutual action plan template showing milestones and owners.
- Short list of recommended quantization profiles for your model family.

If that sounds right I’ll drop the repo link and invite the Thursday workshop.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (text/markdown), sample-toolcall-spec.json (application/json), acme-network-diagram.png (image/png)

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightpath.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK quickstart, tool-calling & embeddings test harness

Thanks Priya — this is excellent and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For auth: we prefer short-lived signed tokens that tie to internal session IDs rather than long-lived static keys. Is there a short snippet to mint those locally for the quickstart?
- Tool calling: the stub looks fine; can it return both structured JSON and a plain-text fallback so the UI can display an explanation when the tool fails?
- Embeddings: yes to a 100–200 record smoke test. We have a de-identified set we can share under our pilot NDA.

We can do Thursday 10am PT. Devon will invite the infra person (Jae) to answer the firewall questions.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product | BrightPath Health
samir@brightpath.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Looping in a couple implementation notes from our SDK team before the Thursday workshop: 

Notes for the quickstart repo
- Python package: include a Dockerfile with a small fake backend (Flask) that exposes /patient and the /tool/resolve endpoints. Keep the dataset under data/sample_records.json.
- TS sample: a Vite-based front-end that demonstrates a tool call + structured JSON rendering and a plain-text fallback path.
- Auth helper: add a utility that mints a short-lived JWT (signed by a local dev key) so Samir can see the token flow without hitting KMS in the pilot.
- Routing: include a config example for pinning to private vs hosted model endpoints (env var RW_TARGET=private|hosted) and a small switch in the SDK to prefer low-latency private pods when available.

Pre-work for Acme (Devon/Samir)
- Share the de-id sample for embeddings (S3 link or Drive).
- Confirm if the pilot subnet can initiate outbound TLS 443 to *.redwood.ai. If not, provide the NAT IPs and we’ll coordinate.

I’ll draft a one-page mutual action plan after the call and assign owners. Priya — I can take the sample front-end and wire up the structured output rendering. Karthik — can you prep the local JWT helper?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
